record.paper_title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds
record.context_brief: Zero in the spectrum for universal covers
record.original_question: Let M̃ be the universal covering of an aspherical closed Riemannian manifold M, equipped with the lifted Riemannian metric. Must zero belong to the spectrum of the minimal closure of the Laplacian on square-integrable smooth p-forms on M̃ for at least one degree p >= 0?

evidence.quote:
Let M̃ be a complete Riemannian manifold. Suppose that M̃ is the universal covering of an aspherical closed Riemannian manifold M (with the Riemannian metric coming from M). Then for some p ≥ 0 zero is in the Spectrum of the minimal closure
(∆p)min : dom((∆p)min) ⊂ L2Ωp(M̃) → L2Ωp(M̃)
of the Laplacian acting on smooth p-forms on M̃.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed aspherical Riemannian manifold (i.e., a closed connected smooth manifold whose universal cover is contractible), and let $\widetilde{M}$ denote its universal cover, equipped with the Riemannian metric lifted from $M$. For each integer $p \ge 0$, let $\Delta_p$ denote the Laplace–Beltrami operator acting on smooth $p$-forms on $\widetilde{M}$, and let $(\Delta_p)_{\min}$ denote its minimal closure as an unbounded self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space $L^2\Omega^p(\widetilde{M})$ of square-integrable $p$-forms.

Prove or disprove: there exists some $p \ge 0$ such that $0$ belongs to the spectrum of $(\Delta_p)_{\min}$.
artifact.category_tag: L^2 spectral geometry of aspherical manifolds
artifact.status_search_result: Farber and Weinberger disproved Lott's general zero-in-the-spectrum conjecture for arbitrary closed manifolds (constructing counterexamples in dimensions ≥ 6), but the version restricted to universal covers of closed aspherical manifolds remains open and is implied by the Strong Novikov Conjecture. Subsequent work (e.g., by Nowak and others) gives partial results under additional hypotheses on the fundamental group, but no general proof or counterexample is known in the aspherical case.

status_evidence.title: On the zero-in-the-spectrum conjecture (Farber–Weinberger)
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples to Lott's general zero-in-the-spectrum conjecture exist in dimensions ≥ 6, but the aspherical case is not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: The general (non-aspherical) version was disproved, but the aspherical version remained open.

status_evidence.title: Zero-in-the-spectrum conjecture on regular covers of compact manifolds (Nowak)
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture for aspherical manifolds is implied by the Strong Novikov Conjecture; partial results under largeness/exactness assumptions on fundamental groups.
status_evidence.claim: The aspherical zero-in-the-spectrum question remains open and is reduced to or implied by other major conjectures.

status_evidence.title: The zero-in-the-spectrum question (Lott survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing the question and its status for various classes of manifolds including aspherical ones.
status_evidence.claim: Lott's survey treats the aspherical case as an open question.
